# Package Dependency Tree Inspection

Tools that show what Python packages are installed and why, revealing the
dependency tree that `pip freeze` flattens.

## Tool Landscape

| Tool | Version | Python | License | Stars | Output Formats |
|------|---------|--------|---------|-------|----------------|
| pipdeptree | 2.35.1 (Apr 2026) | >=3.10 | MIT | 3,000 | text, JSON, Mermaid, Graphviz SVG [1][2] |
| deptry | 0.25.1 (Mar 2026) | >=3.10 | MIT | — | text (violations) [3][4] |
| FawltyDeps | 0.20.0 (Jun 2025) | — | — | 280 | text [26] |
| pip-tree | — | — | — | — | JSON [38] |
| uv tree | built-in (0.5.0+) | — | — | — | text [27] |
| poetry show --tree | built-in | — | — | — | text [36] |

## pipdeptree

The most established tool for visualizing installed package dependency trees
[1][2]. Maintained under the tox-dev organization (Bernát Gábor), with 61
releases and Production/Stable status [1].

**Key capabilities:**
- Default text tree showing parent-child relationships with version constraints
- Reverse dependency lookup (`--reverse --packages <name>`) answering "why is
  this installed?" [2]
- Conflict and circular dependency detection [2]
- Package filtering (`-p PACKAGES`) [2]

**Output formats:** text (default), JSON (`-o json`), Mermaid (`-o mermaid`),
Graphviz SVG (`-o graphviz-svg > deps.svg`) [1][2].

**Limitation:** only inspects installed packages — cannot resolve or preview
uninstalled dependency trees [2].

## deptry

Scans Python files and compares imported modules against declared dependencies
[3][4]. Detects four violation types:

| Code | Violation | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| DEP001 | Missing | Imported but not declared [4] |
| DEP002 | Unused | Declared but not imported [4] |
| DEP003 | Dev in main | Dev dependency used in main code [4] |
| DEP004 | Misplaced | Main dependency declared as dev [4] |

Supports Poetry, pip, PDM, uv, and PEP 621 projects [5]. Configuration via
CLI args or `[tool.deptry]` in pyproject.toml [4]. Must be installed within
the project's virtual environment for proper package metadata access [4].

## FawltyDeps

From Tweag, detects undeclared and unused 3rd-party dependencies [26]. Similar
scope to deptry but different detection approach. 1,061 commits and 28 releases
indicate active maintenance [26].

## Package Manager Built-in Commands

**uv tree:** Added in uv 0.5.0, shows dependency tree from lockfile [27].
Supports `--depth` flag and `--outdated` to highlight packages with newer
versions available.

**poetry show --tree:** Displays dependencies in tree format, with `--why`
flag showing whether packages are direct or required by others [36].

## Gaps and Limitations

- pipdeptree inspects only installed packages, not declared dependencies [2]
- deptry false positives with src layouts (flags project's own package as
  transitive dependency) and PEP 420 namespace packages [counter-discovery]
- No tool combines dependency tree visualization with security auditing in a
  single pass
- pip-tree has limited adoption compared to pipdeptree [38]
